name: Arithmetic overflow / underflow or unchecked cast
requires: solidity <0.8.0 without SafeMath, or >=0.8.0 with an unchecked block
an arithmetic result that feeds a balance, share, price, or accounting write
a value the caller can push toward the boundary
questions: Is the pragma below 0.8.0, and does every arithmetic site on value use SafeMath, or only some?
Where a 0.8.0 contract uses unchecked{}, what bounds the operands there?
Is any uint256 narrowed by a cast to uint128/uint96/uint64/uint32 without a range check first?
Does a downcast silently truncate a user-supplied or oracle-supplied amount?
At the boundary, does the wrap produce a number the code later treats as valid credit?
Is the wrapped value a balance, a debt, a share count, or a loop bound?
Can the caller reach the boundary in one transaction, or does it need many?
Does a require() on the result sit before the write, or after the value has already moved?
false_positives: The pragma is >=0.8.0 and the block is not unchecked, so the compiler reverts
SafeMath wraps every arithmetic site on that variable
The cast is guarded by a prior bounds check that the same value cannot violate
The wrapped value is only a display column, not accounting
Reaching the boundary needs a supply the token cannot reach in the test window
poc_must_show: a before/after balance delta that moves in the attacker's favour, measured on a fork
a control run at a non-boundary value showing normal behaviour
the exact operand pair that wraps, printed
impact_bar: Reportable when the wrap moves real value to an unprivileged caller, with the amount quantified. Informational for a wrap reachable only by an already-privileged role or with no value consequence.
